title: Ventilation/Perfusion PET/CT with Galligas and 68Ga-MAA for regional lung function assessment after pulmonary embolism
official: Ventilation/Perfusion PET/CT with Galligas and 68Ga-MAA for regional lung function assessment after pulmonary embolism
summary: Main objective: To assess the impact of PR on regional perfusion lung function with lung V/Q PET/CT imaging.

interventions.name: PULMOTEC, Creuset de graphite pour la préparation de Technegas pour inhalation
Pulmocis 2 mg trousse pour préparation radiopharmaceutique

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. -Age ≥ 18 years
2. -Patient treated with at least 3 months and up to 8 months of anticoagulation for an acute symptomatic PE diagnosed according the ESC and ACCP guidelines.
3. -Patients who have a PembQol score ≥ 10% and whose total scores for the subgroups Q1 (dyspnea) and Q4 (impact of daily life) are ≥ 10%.
4. -Patients planned to be randomized.
5. -Abnormal conventional V/Q scan at V1
6. -Give consent to participate to the EOLE study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. - Previsible inability to perform the effort test and/or PR
2. - Cardiac insufficiency (unstable coronary artery disease)
3. - Severe respiratory failure (long-term oxygen therapy, pulmonary hypertension)
4. - Chronic dyspnea MMRC ≥ 2 before PE
5. - Cardiac or respiratory rehabilitation in the previous year
6. - Indication to urgent PR within 6 months at the time of inclusion
7. - Life expectancy of less than 12 months
8. - Inability to give consent
9. - Patient under guardianship or curatorship
10. - Patient deprived of liberty by an administrative or judicial decision
11. - Patient has not social security affiliation or who don’t beneficiary of such social security
12. - Presence of CTEPH according to international guidelines
13. - Incapacity to perform the effort test
14. - Effort test stopped because of hemodynamic intolerance
15. - Cardiac failure discovered after PR work up
16. - Patients treated for acute PE with anticoagulants for more than 8 months
17. - Active cancer or in remission for less than two years
18. - Dyspnea post – COVID due to parenchymal injuries
19. - Post-COVID hyperventilation syndrome without pulmonary vascular perfusion sequelae
20. - Physical or psychological inability to undertake PR
21. - Isolated or more distal segmental PE
22. - Neuro-muscular disease with PR contraindication.
